hypothesis: Subject-disjoint training on 7.16 hours of unique motion plus an analytic C2 residual envelope will improve transfer and derivative continuity beyond the strongest procedural shape control, unlike the 17.1-minute unconstrained fits.
controlled_changes: Replace the frozen 78-clip/17.1-minute training set with the 1,840-clip/7.16-hour subject-disjoint train split.
For boundary-only contextual windows, predict residuals over the exact strongest projected shape reference.
Multiply every learned residual channel by a normalized cubic-on-each-side envelope with zero value, slope and curvature at authored observations.
held_constant: The original 394 observed-only condition schema and 153-channel semantic pose representation.
The 128-wide six-block temporal convolution and pure NumPy export path.
AdamW settings, direct loss terms, two fixed seeds, gap set, partial-priority patterns and protected quality gates.
No style conditioning in this experiment; style tags remain recorded for a later separately controlled comparison.

data.sampling: Subject uniform, then clip uniform within subject, then start uniform within clip. Gap/context balanced by deterministic step cycle; patterns 0,1,2 balanced within each batch.
data.window_materialization: Current batch only from memory-mapped positions and rotations.

training.loss: unknown position MSE + 0.1 rotation6 MSE + 0.01 velocity MSE + 0.0001 acceleration MSE using actual seconds
training.selection: Fixed final step only; no development checkpoint selection

evaluation.confirmation: All protected confirmation clips remain sealed unless both seeds pass every development gate.
